_read_me_first: REFERENCE FILE — this whole document is not uploadable as-is.
It documents both upload formats in one place. To upload, copy the value of
Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and appear in no real upload.
Two working files sit beside this one: sample-question-set.json and
sample-practice-test.json. Both are valid and can be uploaded directly.
_the_one_thing_that_will_bite_you: JSON eats backslashes. Every LaTeX command needs a DOUBLE backslash in the file.
Write  \\frac{1}{3}  in the JSON to get  \frac{1}{3}  in the question.
Write  \\sqrt{x}    in the JSON to get  \sqrt{x}    in the question.
A single backslash is either a JSON syntax error or a silently wrong escape.
If a question renders with the command name showing as literal text, this is why.
_math_is_written_in_latex: Wrap every mathematical expression in single dollar signs: $x^{2} + 1$.
Text outside the dollars renders as normal prose. Keep prose OUTSIDE the dollars —
$If x = 2$ renders the word 'If' in italic maths font, which looks wrong.
A literal dollar sign (a price) is written \\$ — see the cheatsheet below.
Nothing converts this for you: what you write is what students see.

_math_cheatsheet._columns: what you want  ->  what to type inside the $...$  ->  what to write in the JSON file

fraction (stacked, one third).never_write: 1/3  — renders as a flat slash and looks unfinished

pi.never_write: pi  — renders as the two letters p and i

multiplication.never_write: *  — an asterisk is not a multiplication sign

exponent.note: Always brace the exponent. x^10 renders as x¹0; x^{10} renders as x¹⁰.

a percent sign INSIDE maths.why: A bare % starts a comment in LaTeX and silently swallows the rest of the line.

a dollar sign (a price).why: A bare $ opens a maths span and swallows the sentence up to the next $. Prices are prose — keep them OUTSIDE any $...$ and escape them.

_domains_and_subtopics._note: domain and subtopic are matched case-insensitively, by name or by slug. An unknown pair is rejected with a reason unless create_new_subtopics is true.

_field_reference.external_id: Required. Your own id, unique within the set. Re-uploading a file skips rows whose external_id already exists in that set, so uploads are repeatable. Max 64 chars.
_field_reference.domain: Required. One of the four above. Max 100 chars.
_field_reference.subtopic: Required. Must belong to that domain, unless create_new_subtopics is true. Max 120 chars.
_field_reference.choices: Required. Exactly four, labelled exactly A, B, C and D. Order in the file does not matter; storage sorts by label. Each text max 1000 chars.
_field_reference.explanation: Required. Shown after answering, and on the practice test review screen. Max 4000 chars.
_field_reference.module_number: PRACTICE TESTS ONLY. 1 or 2. Omit entirely from a question set upload.
_field_reference._limits: 500 questions per question-set upload, 1 MB per file. A practice test is exactly 22 or 44.

question_set_upload._this_is_the_uploadable_shape: Copy this object into its own .json file and upload it at /admin/questions.
question_set_upload.set_description: Optional. Only applied when the set is first created.

questions.prompt: If $\frac{1}{3}x - 2 = 5$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Add $2$ to both sides to get $\frac{1}{3}x = 7$, then multiply both sides by $3$: $x = 21$.

questions.prompt: The volume of a cone is $V = \frac{1}{3} \cdot \pi \cdot r^{2} \cdot h$. What is the volume of a cone with radius $3$ and height $4$?
A jacket costs \$250. Its price is increased by $20\%$. What is the new price, in dollars?
questions.explanation: $20\%$ of \$250 is \$50, so the new price is \$250 + \$50 = \$300. Note the prices sit outside the maths and are written with an escaped dollar sign.

questions.prompt: A line passes through $(-2, 1)$ and $(2, 7)$. What is its slope?
questions.explanation: Slope is the change in $y$ over the change in $x$: $\frac{7 - 1}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}$.

practice_test_upload._this_is_the_uploadable_shape: Copy this object into its own .json file. Create the test at /admin/practice-tests FIRST, then upload the questions on that test's page.
practice_test_upload._there_is_no_set_name_here: A practice test names its own question set automatically, from the test title you typed in the admin form.
practice_test_upload._counts_are_enforced_exactly: A FULL test needs exactly 22 questions with module_number 1 and exactly 22 with module_number 2. A HALF test needs exactly 22 with module_number 1 and none with 2. A wrong count rejects the whole file and imports nothing — it reports what it found against what it expected.

questions.prompt: If $5x - 3 = 17$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Add $3$ to both sides to get $5x = 20$, then divide both sides by $5$: $x = 4$.

questions.prompt: In right triangle $ABC$, the right angle is at $C$, the side opposite $\angle A$ has length $5$, and the hypotenuse has length $13$. What is $\sin(A)$?
questions.explanation: $\sin$ is opposite over hypotenuse. The side opposite $\angle A$ is $5$ and the hypotenuse is $13$, so $\sin(A) = \frac{5}{13}$.
